L3.findings: 1) The scenario's premise (FAST waits its limit and gives up) does not happen. FAST's limit runs to SLOW's 60-minute point (11:50, 12 minutes after FAST's start, within 20). At 11:50 FAST finds SLOW's record Started and 60 minutes old, closes it Failed and takes the lease while SLOW is still running, so two runs can write at once. SLOW's closing write can also overwrite the Failed mark. 2) SLOW's only guard is 'Start no new row 40 minutes after you hold the lease or 45 minutes after your start ... (your record must close before it turns stale at 60)'. Nothing makes SLOW stop and close its record by a fixed time (say 55 minutes). A row started at 11:34 can run past 11:50. So 'a live run never reaches 60 minutes with its record open' is not guaranteed.
L3.notes: Literal path: FAST 11:38 reads SLOW (Started 10:50, 48 minutes old): held. Re-checks at 11:40 ... 11:48 and, because 'until the holder's record turns 60 minutes old if that comes within 20 minutes of your start' applies, also at 11:50. There 'one Started 60 minutes ago or more is stale: set it Failed ... and it holds nothing'. FAST holds, confirms at 11:51 and sends the G reply; the row ends as in G. To answer the question as framed: if FAST did give up (for example, if SLOW's record were under 60 minutes old at the end of FAST's wait), it would write only its own run record ('end Partial "lease held by SLOW <run id>" with no row written'). It would not log the inbound or write a reply segment ('While it does, only read'). The row would stay as found: Next date 2026-11-02, Waiting on [Guest or PR, Akshay], Next action unchanged. The reply action would stay due for the next FAST run (12:38) through STEP 1's unanswered-thread scan, with owner and Next date unchanged.

I2a.findings: The old segment 'Zoya: send next steps to Jheel' is keyed by FAST ('Any other old-format segment still unkeyed is FAST's to key by the fixed keying rules on the developer page'). Those rules aren't visible here. ACTIONS says to build the raised time from 'the Activity or message that created it, and its Claude note date'. That could be the inbound's 09:55 or the inbox's 10:20, while STEP 1 keys the same ask at the message time. Inside one FAST run the Sent check covers a mismatch, but the key isn't provably unique.
I2a.notes: Case a: FAST's record is 0.5 s earlier. If both are in second 10:50:00 it's a tie and goes to FAST; if not, FAST is earlier. Either way FAST holds and SLOW backs off and waits. Only FAST acts: the step is type reply ('a mailed sponsored yes is yours'). It keys and writes the key onto the segment before acting, then sends one 'Sponsored yes: next steps' (To Jheel, Cc Akshay, Jaya, Sarika) with idempotency_key = the action key, logs it and completes the segment. SLOW later holds; its RECONCILE sees the action complete, and it never sends FAST's types ('never a send of FAST's types'). One mail. What prevents a second: the lease first, then the type split, then the Activity Action key and Sent/thread check, then idempotency_key.

I2b.findings: 1) The lease doesn't stop a second FAST run. Each run reads only the other kind's records ('read the latest run record with Source ID starting "run:zoya:slow:"'). So the scheduled run and the manual re-fire both 'hold' and write the same row at once. That breaks 'exactly one run holds the lease at any time'. 2) Only idempotency_key prevents a duplicate send: both runs derive the same action key and pass it to email_compose or the draft send. That relies on (a) MCP Emails honouring the key across sessions and drafts, and (b) both runs keying the old-format segment the same way (see the I2a finding). The Activity and Sent/thread checks can race: run 2 can check before run 1's send lands. 3) Both runs can create a draft ('never a second draft' can't hold under a race), and both can try to log the Activity. MESSAGE IDENTITY's lookup-before-create also races. 4) Both WRITE PATH row writes can collide; the re-read repairs only a missing segment, not duplicates.
I2b.notes: Case b: FAST 11:38:00 and FAST 11:38:20 each find no SLOW record holding, so each holds. Both see the same due reply. Run 1 sends with idempotency_key = the reply action key. Run 2's Activity check may run before run 1 logs, and its Sent check may run before run 1's send lands; its send carries the same key, so the provider should return the first send rather than send again. Canon assumes the provider dedupes: 1 mail, row as in G. Without provider dedupe, it would be 2 mails and 2 drafts.

RECONCILE runs only when FAST has no record in 90 minutes or a reply action over 2 hours old is incomplete; neither is true here. The send, the inbound and the row move are never recorded. The row stays Sponsored offered, 'Waiting on Jheel: reply to the sponsored commercials', which risks a sponsored follow-up after a yes on 2 Nov. SLOW 10:50 sees it at 12 to 37 minutes old and gives up at 11:15, before it goes stale at 11:38 (48 minutes after SLOW's start is outside the 20-minute extension). FAST 11:38 reads only 'run:zoya:slow:' records. Later SLOW runs read only FAST's latest record, which is 11:38's. So the 10:38 record stays Started for good. 3) SLOW 10:50 waits 25 minutes and ends Partial with nothing due in scope. 4) Side note: the pre-existing send had only Akshay in Cc, without Jaya and Sarika, which revenue mail requires. Recovery can't repair that.
